new_value: L76K NMEA validation suite landed (commits fc5977b5b9 + b42d16895e, lichen/tests/nmea_l76k, 4 files, 100% suite PASS on native_sim/native/64): feeds Quectel L76K datasheet-style output through Zephyr's gnss_nmea0183_parse_rmc/parse_gga and verifies lat ~22.5715N / lon ~114.0246E (nanodegree range checks, 0.01-deg window), UTC 06:48:23 + date fields (h/m/day/month/year), altitude 80600 mm, satellites 12, HDOP 680 (1/1000), GSV variable-field overflow safety, PMTK proprietary prefix recognition. The splitter mirrors modem_chat's wildcard separators (',' and '*') with checksum stripping and bound-checked token emission, so argv/argc match what the production AG3335-pattern driver passes. Verification: native_sim/native/64 build green, ztest 4/4 PASS (RMC/GGA/PMTK/GSV), sanitizers via the testcase chain. Codereview delegated to kimi-k3 (consolidated + verdict pass) found 4 issues, ALL fixed: [P2] GNSS_SATELLITES=y unused -> removed (GNSS_NMEA0183 selects what it needs), [P2] inline splitter had no MAX_TOKENS bound (latent stack overflow) -> single shared bound-checked helper replacing 4 copies, [P2] checksum stayed fused to the final token ('V*14') diverging from modem_chat's '*'-separator behavior -> stripped, [P3] dead split_nmea helper removed. Root-cause chain during verification: the parse functions take argv INCLUDING the '$GNTOK' address token (Zephyr reference test convention) — my first harness dropped it shifting all fields; a splitter off-by-one (tokens[count] after count++) then masked the fix; both corrected. Scope notes: Zephyr's GGA parser handles altitude/HDOP/satellites only (position via RMC) — asserted and documented in-suite; interleaved multi-line GSV overflow safety covered by the variable-fields case. Unblocks sibling sxvf (L76K driver).
